title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
technique: RadixAttention (radix-tree LRU KV reuse across calls) + cache-aware scheduling + compressed FSM for constrained decoding + API speculative execution, with a frontend DSL for LM programs

optimized_metrics.evidence: We design a cache-aware scheduling algorithm to increase the cache hit rate.
executing LM programs is inefficient due to redundant computation and memory usage; requests with the same prompt prefix can reuse the KV cache, reducing redundant computation and memory usage

headline_claim.text: SGLang achieves up to 6.4x higher throughput compared to state-of-the-art inference systems on various large language and multi-modal models on tasks including agent control, logical reasoning, few-shot learning benchmarks, JSON decoding, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and multi-turn chat.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 6 (normalized latency, one program at a time)
Fig 8a/b 'first token latency'; Chatbot Arena 1.7x reduction
constrained decoding / API speculative execution accuracy (§6, appendix)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For throughput, we run a sufficiently large batch of program instances to compute the maximum throughput, comparing the number of program instances executed per second (programs per second, p/s).
metric_definitions.notes: Unit is LM programs/s (each program has several LLM calls), not tokens/s; offline max-throughput regime.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: For latency, we execute a single program at a time without batching and report the average latency for multiple instances.
metric_definitions.notes: Batch-1, no queueing: whole-program latency, not per-request TTFT/TPOT.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define the cache hit rate as number of cached prompt tokens / number of prompt tokens.
metric_definitions.locator: §3 Cache-aware scheduling; appendix: sum over requests of cached prefill tokens / sum of prefill tokens

metric_definitions.definition_quote: RadixAttention also reduces the computation of prefill, thus decreasing the first token latency.
metric_definitions.notes: Used (Fig 8, production) without a formal definition.

load_regime: offline batch (large batch of program instances for throughput); batch=1 sequential for latency; no request-rate sweep
tradeoff_acknowledged: Greedy cache-aware (longest-shared-prefix-first) scheduling 'can lead to starvation' (fairness), left as future work; in latency-sensitive settings only limited re-ordering tolerated.
workloads: MMLU, HellaSwag, ReAct/agent, tree-of-thought, JSON decoding, DSPy RAG, multi-turn chat, ShareGPT; Chatbot Arena production
extractor_notes: Throughput unit is programs/s, unusual vs tokens/s in the other papers. Latency is batch-1 whole-program mean. First-token latency used in Fig 8 and production claim without definition. Optimizes cache-hit rate as an intermediate proxy.
